proposals.title: CanonicalEncoder third attempt: resolve three specific review-02 blockers
proposals.why_now: TASK-0005 has been rejected twice. Review-02 identified exactly three MAJOR findings: cyclic containers cause uncontrolled native stack overflow rather than CanonicalEncoderError (REVIEW-001), plain-object accessor hostile tests are absent (REVIEW-002), and compile plus boundary-check evidence is not independently captured (REVIEW-003). These are narrowly scoped, well-specified fixes. The encoder must be accepted before StateHash can exist, and StateHash is required for INV-01 and INV-22 which are FASE-1 acceptance criteria. All other FASE-1 hash-dependent deliverables remain gated on this single acceptance.

proposals.title: Branded numeric types and division helper (ADR-003 + ADR-004 foundation)
proposals.why_now: The branded numeric types — Money, Quantity, Price, Rate as bigint; Tick and safe-integer coordinates as number — are the primitive vocabulary of every subsequent FASE-1 deliverable: ledger entries, price queries, RNG coordinates, and the tick loop. No price generator, no ledger, and no order execution can be implemented without these types being in packages/core. This work is independent of the CanonicalEncoder and can proceed in parallel. ADR-004 requires that every division declares a rounding mode; establishing the helper and the lint rule that enforces it now avoids retrofitting across all future arithmetic code.

proposals.title: Positional RNG (ADR-002): hash function ADR and rand() implementation
proposals.why_now: The price generator, macro event scheduler, bot policy derivation, and NPC tip truth all depend on rand(masterSeed, namespace, ...coordinates). This function must be implemented before any world output can be tested or any INV-02 or INV-03 invariant can be verified. The hash function used inside rand() is a DEFINIR item requiring an ADR with bit-exact specification; the spec recommends SplitMix64 over FNV-1a accumulator. This work is independent of the CanonicalEncoder and can proceed in parallel.

proposals.title: Electron security scaffolding and minimum installer (INV-29, FASE-1 CI requirement)
proposals.why_now: FASE-1 acceptance explicitly requires a minimum installer for Windows and Linux produced by CI, a dedicated simulation worker, and INV-29 (contextIsolation, nodeIntegration:false, sandbox:true) verified by the CI gate. The spec warns that discovering packaging and ABI problems at the end of the project is unrecoverable. The monorepo stubs for main, preload, renderer, and simulation-worker exist but are empty. This Electron scaffolding work is fully independent of the canonical encoder and numeric type work and can proceed in any order. Every day it is delayed is a day of reduced ability to test the worker IPC contract that the domain simulation depends on.

proposals.title: StateHash: hash function ADR and implementation in packages/core
proposals.why_now: StateHash is required by INV-01, INV-22, and multiple FASE-1 acceptance criteria. The spec mandates ADR-009 and the CanonicalEncoder be complete before any StateHash implementation exists. Once the encoder is accepted (IDEA-001), StateHash is the immediate next step: it specifies which fields enter the hash, which are explicitly excluded (finalTick, narrative text), and how the hash function is applied to canonical bytes. Delaying the StateHash ADR decision after encoder acceptance will block the replay CLI and the CI gate that compares StateHash by tick.
